NAME: Event Batch Validator
DESC:
A partner sends purchase events in batches through an API. Before loading a batch into the warehouse, your job validates every record against the expected schema, normalizes the valid ones and produces a load report. You do not make real HTTP calls: the API is given to you as a function.

API

fetch_batch() takes no argument and returns a dict such as:

{
    "batch_id": "b-001",
    "records": [
        {"event_id": "e1", "user_id": 42, "amount": 19.99, "currency": "mad", "ts": "2024-03-05T10:00:00Z"},
        ...
    ]
}

records may be null or empty, and an element of records is not guaranteed to be a JSON object. fetch_batch can raise an exception. Call fetch_batch exactly once.

Schema and rules

Records are validated one by one, in order. For each record, the checks below are applied in this order, and the first failed check gives the rejection reason. A field is missing if its key is absent or its value is null. Keys that are not in the schema are ignored.

order field rule reason if missing reason if invalid
0 (record) must be a JSON object (a dict) not_an_object
1 event_id required; a string that is not empty after trimming; stored trimmed missing_event_id invalid_event_id
2 user_id required; an integer (a boolean is not an integer) or a string of digits (after trimming), converted to int; must be > 0 missing_user_id invalid_user_id
3 amount required; a number (not a boolean) or a numeric string (after trimming), converted to float; must be finite and >= 0; stored rounded to 2 decimals missing_amount invalid_amount
4 currency optional: if missing, "EUR"; otherwise a string that is exactly 3 letters A-Z after trimming and converting to uppercase; stored normalized invalid_currency
5 ts required; a string in the exact format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (UTC, T and Z literal) that represents a real date and time; stored unchanged missing_ts invalid_ts
6 event_id must not be equal to the event_id of a record already loaded from this batch duplicate_event_id

A record that passes all checks is loaded.

Output

A dict with exactly these keys:

key type description
status str "ok", or "error" if fetch_batch raised an exception
error str or None name of the exception class (e.g. "TimeoutError"), None when status is ok
batch_id str or None batch_id of the response, None on error
read int number of elements in records
loaded int number of loaded records
rejected int number of rejected records
rejections dict[str, int] number of rejected records per reason; reasons with no rejected record do not appear
records list[dict] loaded records in input order, each with exactly the keys event_id, user_id, amount, currency, ts

On error, the counters are 0, rejections is {} and records is [].

Example

fetch_batch() returns:

{
    "batch_id": "b-001",
    "records": [
        {"event_id": "e1", "user_id": 42, "amount": 19.99, "currency": "mad", "ts": "2024-03-05T10:00:00Z"},
        {"event_id": "e2", "user_id": "43", "amount": "5", "ts": "2024-03-05T10:01:00Z"},
        {"event_id": "e3", "user_id": True, "amount": 1, "ts": "2024-03-05T10:02:00Z"},
        {"event_id": "e1", "user_id": 44, "amount": 2.5, "currency": "EUR", "ts": "2024-03-05T10:03:00Z"},
        {"user_id": 45, "amount": 3, "ts": "2024-03-05T10:04:00Z"},
        {"event_id": "e6", "user_id": 46, "amount": -1, "ts": "2024-03-05T10:05:00Z"},
        "e7,47,9.5",
        {"event_id": "e8", "user_id": 48, "amount": 7.5, "currency": "euro", "ts": "2024-03-05 10:06:00"},
        {"event_id": "e9", "user_id": 49, "amount": 0, "currency": None, "ts": "2024-02-30T10:00:00Z", "extra": "x"},
    ],
}

{
    "status": "ok",
    "error": None,
    "batch_id": "b-001",
    "read": 9,
    "loaded": 2,
    "rejected": 7,
    "rejections": {
        "invalid_user_id": 1, "duplicate_event_id": 1, "missing_event_id": 1, "invalid_amount": 1,
        "not_an_object": 1, "invalid_currency": 1, "invalid_ts": 1,
    },
    "records": [
        {"event_id": "e1", "user_id": 42, "amount": 19.99, "currency": "MAD", "ts": "2024-03-05T10:00:00Z"},

Function signature

def ingest_events(fetch_batch) -> dict:
    ...

Constraints

  • Standard library only (json, math, re, datetime, ... are available).
  • A batch contains up to 10^5 records.

The functions described in the task (the API) are provided by the tests: you only write your function.
